_comment: Claude Code MCP configuration — canonical memory control plane and Context7 docs.
Authority: environment/agents/adapters/claude-code/mcp.template.json is the
SINGLE canonical owner. The project-scope .mcp.json is RENDERED from this file
by ops/scripts/claude_projection.py (domain: mcp) and drift-checked — it is a
projection, never a second authority.
NO CREDENTIAL VALUES in this file, in .mcp.json, or in the account variables
field. A remote server's credential is bound from Infisical at spawn by a
local bridge (ops/secrets/vault_mcp_bridge.py) and never written down;
a ${VAR} reference remains only for values the host itself supplies.
_requires_env on a server: the server renders only when every listed variable
is set and non-empty. _optional_headers: {VAR: {header: value}} merges those
headers only when VAR is set and non-empty. Both are private keys, stripped
from the render like _comment. Use them for a server that has a working
fallback when its credential is absent.
context7 is deliberately NOT _requires_env-gated: a gated server turned a
missing secret into a silently absent one. It is a local stdio BRIDGE
(ops/secrets/run_vault_mcp_bridge.sh context7 -> vault_mcp_bridge.py) that
binds CONTEXT7_API_KEY from Infisical in-process, as this surface's machine
identity, and forwards to https://mcp.context7.com/mcp. The key is never in
the environment, argv, .mcp.json or a file. An unbound key makes the bridge
refuse to start and name the fix (L9_INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET); SessionStart
reports the bind either way.
l9-graphite-memory is the ONLY memory server (MemoryService over stdio;
memory-control-plane/v1). command is the spawn wrapper at
${HOME}/.cursor-governance/ops/memory/run_memory_mcp.sh — Claude Code
expands ${HOME} at load (set by the OS on Dock launch). The wrapper
bind-proves L9_MEMORY_INTERPRETER via runtime_binding, so a desktop
session does not need that variable in the parent env. The wrapper is
the bind gate; this entry is not _requires_env-gated on the interpreter.
The legacy direct-provider front door (graphiti-memory over a
provider URL) was retired at realignment stage C8: Cursor-Governance
no longer knows how to call the provider, and the session hooks
(memory_prefetch / memory_writeback) reach memory through ops/memory only.
ADDING AN MCP SERVER: add its entry here (this file is the only authority for
Claude Code), reference every credential as ${VAR} under _requires_env or
_optional_headers, then `make claude-projection` renders .mcp.json and
`make claude-desktop-install` renders Claude Desktop from environment/mcp/master.mcp.json.
STILL FORBIDDEN: a literal token value anywhere in this file or in the account
variables field, the retired HTTP l9-shared-memory side door, L9_MEMORY_HTTP_*
lifecycle env, any direct provider URL or bearer, and
${L9_CAPABILITY_BROKER_URL}/mcp/graphiti (never shipped).
_retired_servers lists keys this template used to manage and has withdrawn;
the projection removes them from .mcp.json instead of preserving them as
consumer-owned.

l9-graphite-memory._owner: l9-graphite-memory: args stay the package's managed_server_entry (client_config/cursor.py); command is the bootstrap spawn wrapper so Claude Code desktop can launch without L9_MEMORY_INTERPRETER in the parent env. tests/ops/memory/test_mcp_surfaces.py holds the wrapper command and package args. No secret values in this template (ADR-016). ADR-0031 assertion env (L9_MEMORY_AGENTS_DOOR_SECRET / L9_MEMORY_AGENT_ASSERTION / the launching principal's own signing-key and grant JSON) must already be present in the environment Claude Code is started with — a pre-launch handoff, e.g. `source ops/memory/export_agent_assertion_env.sh` in the launching shell. The server inherits Claude's environment; a SessionStart hook is a child of Claude and cannot inject into it, and this file never carries an env block or a secret. When the handoff is absent the SessionStart context reports the signed-agent door UNAVAILABLE.
